entries.name: mcp__plugin_datadog_mcp__analyze_datadog_logs
entries.description: Analyze Datadog logs using SQL. Runs against a virtual 'logs' table filtered by your search query. Good for aggregations, counts, group-bys, or peeking at recent logs with LIMIT. To discover custom attributes for extra_columns, first call search_datadog_logs with extra_fields. If a query times out, try a shorter time range. MUST load the datadog/ddsql skill before calling this tool.

extra_columns.description: Extend the logs table with additional typed columns. To discover available attributes, call search_datadog_logs with extra_fields (e.g. ['*'] or ['http*']), then declare them here. Key translation from search response keys to extra_columns names: strip the bucket prefix and prepend '@' — `custom.X` → `{name: "@X"}`, `attributes.X` → `{name: "@X"}`, `error.X` → `{name: "@error.X"}`; tags from the `tags:` list use bare names without '@' — e.g. tag `team:foo` → `{name: "team"}`. Never pass the raw response-prefixed form (e.g. never `custom.X` or `attributes.X`). Supported types: varchar, bigint, decimal, boolean, timestamp, array<varchar>, array<bigint>, array<decimal>, array<boolean>, array<timestamp>.

name.description: Column name in the SQL virtual table.

filter.description: Datadog search query to filter logs before SQL analysis. When relevant services are known, prefer filtering by service name or prefix. Broad queries are fine for discovery or cross-service questions. Use key:value for tags/facets (e.g. 'service:nginx', 'env:prod'), '@' prefix for raw attributes (e.g. '@http.status_code:[400 TO 499]'). Examples: 'service:nginx status:error', 'env:(production OR test) AND -version:beta', 'service:web* foo'. Tip: '(source:foo OR service:foo)' if unsure which field. For severe issues: 'status:(critical OR alert OR emergency)'.

from.description: Start of time window. ISO 8601, Unix epoch ms, or relative ('now-1h').

indexes.description: Restrict to specific log indexes (e.g. ['main', 'pci']). Default: ['*'] (all).

sql_query.description: SQL against the 'logs' table. Examples: 'SELECT count(*) FROM logs', 'SELECT service, count(*) FROM logs GROUP BY service ORDER BY count(*) DESC', 'SELECT status, count(*) FROM logs GROUP BY status', 'SELECT DATE_TRUNC(\'hour\', timestamp) as hour, count(*) FROM logs GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC(\'hour\', timestamp)'. Default columns: timestamp (timestamp), host (string), service (string), env (string), version (string), status (string), message (string); add more via extra_columns. DDSQL (Datadog SQL) is a PostgreSQL subset: every non-aggregated SELECT column must appear in GROUP BY, SELECT aliases cannot be reused in WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING (repeat the full expression instead, e.g., GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('hour', timestamp) not GROUP BY hour), and only declared table columns may be referenced. Use the -> operator or json_extract_path_text (cast as needed) for JSON access. Avoid unsupported constructs like ANY(), ->>, QUALIFY, information_schema, and current_timestamp. Column names containing special characters like '@' must be quoted (e.g., SELECT "@foo" FROM logs). TIME FILTERING: the virtual table already contains only events within the from/to time window — never add WHERE timestamp >= ... in SQL. INTERVAL and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP are not supported and will cause query errors.

storage_tier.description: Storage type: 'indexes' (default, hot only), 'flex_and_indexes' (Flex + hot). online-archives and cloudprem not supported.

intent.description: Briefly describe the wider context task, and why this tool was chosen. Omit argument values, PII/secrets. Use English.

to.description: End of time window. Same formats as 'from'.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_datadog_mcp__search_datadog_logs
entries.description: Search and retrieve raw log entries or log patterns. Do NOT use for counting or aggregations — use analyze_datadog_logs instead. Best for: viewing raw logs, discovering patterns (use_log_patterns=true), and discovering custom attributes via extra_fields for use as extra_columns in analyze_datadog_logs. Response shape (when extra_fields is set, output is YAML): three buckets — (1) top-level fields like env/host/service queried bare (`env:prod`); (2) `attributes:` map with source-prefixed keys — `custom.X` and `attributes.X` are queried as `@X` (strip the bucket prefix), but `error.X` keeps its prefix as `@error.X` because `error` is a real top-level attribute; (3) `tags:` list of `key:value` strings queried bare. Load the datadog/logs skill for the full key-translation table.

clustering_pattern_field.description: Log field used for clustering logs with similar values when use_log_patterns is true. Can cluster on any attribute or tag present in the logs. Consider '@error.message', '@errorMessage', '@error' or '@error.stack' when investigating error logs. Default: 'message'.

extra_fields.description: Extra attributes/tags to include. Use bare names without '@' or prefix (e.g., 'duration', not '@duration' or 'custom.duration'). Supports wildcards ('experiments*', '*' for all). The response shows attribute keys with a display prefix (custom.X, error.X); that prefix signals the translation: custom.X → @X, error.X → @error.X in extra_columns. Load the datadog/logs skill for the full translation table.

from.description: Start of the time range. Accepts ISO 8601 (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' or '2024-01-01'), Unix timestamp (seconds or milliseconds), or relative (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d', 'now'). Default: now-1h.

indexes.description: Restrict to specific log indexes (e.g. ['main', 'pci']). Default: ['*'] (all).

limit.description: Optional maximum number of logs or patterns to return (1-1000). If omitted, results are bounded only by max_tokens.

max_tokens.description: Max tokens in the response. Hard cap: 20000 (values above are clamped, not rejected).

pattern_group_by.description: Only used when use_log_patterns=true. Fields/tags to group patterns by (e.g. ['service', '@env']). Can group by any attribute or tag present in the logs. Each returned pattern will be scoped to a unique combination of these fields, and their values surface in the 'groups' column. Default: no grouping (patterns aggregate across all values).

query.description: Datadog search query. When relevant services are known, prefer filtering by service name or prefix. Broad queries are fine for discovery or cross-service questions. Common tags: service, env, host, source. Prefix raw attributes with '@'. Examples: 'service:nginx status:error', '@http.status_code:[400 TO 499]', 'env:(production OR test) AND -version:beta', 'service:web* foo', '"foo bar"'. Tip: '(source:foo OR service:foo)' if unsure which field. Severe issues: 'status:(critical OR alert OR emergency)'.

storage_tier.description: Storage type. 'flex_and_indexes' (Flex + hot), 'online_archives_and_indexes' (archive + hot). Default: hot only.

intent.description: Briefly describe the wider context task, and why this tool was chosen. Omit argument values, PII/secrets. Use English.

to.description: End of the time range. Accepts ISO 8601 (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' or '2024-01-01'), Unix timestamp (seconds or milliseconds), or relative (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d', 'now'). Default: now.

use_log_patterns.description: When true, returns clusters of logs with similar messages instead of raw logs.

# Can be used to implement more programatic error handling
# https://docs.honeybadger.io/lib/ruby/getting-started/ignoring-errors.html#ignore-programmatically

# rubocop:disable Metrics/BlockLength
Rails.application.reloader.to_prepare do
  message_fingerprints = {
    "Rack::Timeout::RequestTimeoutException" => "rack_timeout",
    "Rack::Timeout::RequestTimeoutError" => "rack_timeout",
    "PG::QueryCanceled" => "pg_query_canceled"
  }

  component_fingerprints = {
    "internal" => "internal"
  }

  honeybadger_exceptions_to_ignore = [
    ActiveRecord::QueryCanceled,
    ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound,
    Pundit::NotAuthorizedError,
    RateLimitChecker::LimitReached,
  ]

  # https://docs.honeybadger.io/lib/ruby/gem-reference/configuration.html
  Honeybadger.configure do |config|
    config.env = "#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}-#{Rails.env}"
    config.api_key = ApplicationConfig["HONEYBADGER_API_KEY"]
    config.revision = ApplicationConfig["RELEASE_FOOTPRINT"]

    # Prevent Ruby from exiting until all queued notices have been delivered to Honeybadger.
    # When set to true(default), it can lead to a large number of errors causing a process to get stuck.
    # To prevent this we set it to false ensuring that a process can exit quickly regardless of errors.
    # Logging allows us to fill in gaps if we need to when errors get discarded.
    config.send_data_at_exit = false

    config.exceptions.ignore += honeybadger_exceptions_to_ignore
    config.request.filter_keys += %w[authorization]
    config.sidekiq.attempt_threshold = 10
    config.breadcrumbs.enabled = true

    config.before_notify do |notice|
      notice.ignore! if notice.error_class == "SignalException" && notice.error_message&.include?("SIGHUP")

      notice.fingerprint = if notice.error_message&.include?("SIGTERM") && notice.component&.include?("feeds_import")
                             notice.error_message
                           elsif (msg_key = message_fingerprints.keys.detect do |k, _v|
                                    notice.error_message&.include?(k)
                                  end)
                             message_fingerprints[msg_key]
                           elsif (cmp_key = component_fingerprints.keys.detect do |k, _v|
                                    notice.component&.include?(k)
                                  end)
                             component_fingerprints[cmp_key]
                           end
    end
  end
end

content.thinking: I've traced the noise: every exception class mapped in `rescue_responses` (RecordNotFound, CSRF, RoutingError, Pundit, in `config/application.rb:116-124`) gets logged as a full ERROR stack trace despite Rails converting them to normal 404/422 responses—accounting for most of the ~880 ERROR lines/minute hitting Datadog. I'll now weigh two fix approaches, which differ in whether Datadog config also needs updating.

options.description: Add a filter to config/initializers/betterstack.rb that drops lines for any class in Rails' rescue_responses, so it keeps up with config/application.rb automatically. Datadog and stdout stay exactly as they are.
options.preview:
Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack do |entry|
  RESCUED.any? { |k| entry.message.to_s.include?("#{k} (") }
end
# RESCUED = ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys

stdout/Datadog: unchanged
Better Stack:   ~450 -> ~25 lines / 15 min

options.label: Everywhere, Rails switch
options.description: Set config.action_dispatch.log_rescued_responses = false (built into Rails, one line). Also removes these lines from stdout, and therefore from Datadog logs. APM still counts the 404s.
options.preview:
# config/application.rb
config.action_dispatch.log_rescued_responses = false

stdout/Datadog: ~880 -> ~50 ERROR lines/min
Better Stack:   ~450 -> ~25 lines / 15 min

options.description: Keep sending everything and exclude these patterns in the Better Stack alert queries instead. No deploy, but you pay to ingest the noise and live tail stays noisy.

require "rails_helper"
require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

RSpec.describe "Better Stack initializer" do # rubocop:disable RSpec/DescribeClass
  let(:initializer_path) { Rails.root.join("config/initializers/betterstack.rb") }
  let(:stdout) { StringIO.new }
  let(:stdout_logger) { ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.new(ActiveSupport::Logger.new(stdout)) }
  let(:rails_logger) { ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger).tap { |logger| logger.level = :error } }
  let(:device) { Betterstack::LogDevice.new("token", flush_continuously: false) }

  before do
    allow(Rails).to receive(:logger).and_return(rails_logger)
    allow(Rails.env).to receive(:production?).and_return(true)
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).and_call_original
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return("token")
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST").and_return("in.logs.example.com")
    allow(ENV).to receive(:fetch).and_call_original
    allow(ENV).to receive(:fetch).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return("token")
    allow(Betterstack::LogDevice).to receive(:new).and_return(device)
    allow(device).to receive(:write).and_return(true)
  end

  it "adds a Better Stack logger at the Rails log level" do
    load initializer_path

    betterstack_logger = rails_logger.broadcasts.last
    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts.first).to be(stdout_logger)
    expect(betterstack_logger).to be_a(Logtail::Logger)
    expect(betterstack_logger.level).to eq(Logger::ERROR)
    expect(Betterstack::LogDevice).to have_received(:new).with("token", ingesting_host: "in.logs.example.com")
  end

  it "sends lines at or above the Rails log level to Better Stack and stdout" do
    load initializer_path

    rails_logger.warn("ignored")
    rails_logger.error("boom")

    expect(device).to have_received(:write).once.with(having_attributes(level: :error, message: "boom"))
    expect(stdout.string).to include("boom")
    expect(stdout.string).not_to include("ignored")
  end

  it "runs tagged blocks, like ActiveJob#perform_now, once" do
    load initializer_path
    runs = 0

    rails_logger.tagged("ActiveJob") do
      runs += 1
      rails_logger.error("inside a job")
    end

    expect(runs).to eq(1)
    expect(device).to have_received(:write).once
    expect(stdout.string).to include("[ActiveJob] inside a job")
  end

  it "falls back to logtail's default host when BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST is unset" do
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST").and_return(nil)

    load initializer_path

    expect(Betterstack::LogDevice).to have_received(:new).with("token", ingesting_host: nil)
  end

  it "does nothing without BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN" do
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return(nil)

    load initializer_path

    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts).to eq([stdout_logger])
  end

  it "does nothing outside production" do
    allow(Rails.env).to receive(:production?).and_return(false)

    load initializer_path

    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts).to eq([stdout_logger])
  end
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set, and the logtail gem isn't loaded otherwise.
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  betterstack_logger.level = Rails.logger.level

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set, and the logtail gem isn't loaded otherwise.
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  betterstack_logger.level = Rails.logger.level

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

require "rails_helper"
require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

RSpec.describe "Better Stack initializer" do # rubocop:disable RSpec/DescribeClass
  let(:initializer_path) { Rails.root.join("config/initializers/betterstack.rb") }
  let(:stdout) { StringIO.new }
  let(:stdout_logger) { ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.new(ActiveSupport::Logger.new(stdout)) }
  let(:rails_logger) { ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger).tap { |logger| logger.level = :error } }
  let(:device) { Betterstack::LogDevice.new("token", flush_continuously: false) }

  before do
    allow(Rails).to receive(:logger).and_return(rails_logger)
    allow(Rails.env).to receive(:production?).and_return(true)
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).and_call_original
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return("token")
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST").and_return("in.logs.example.com")
    allow(ENV).to receive(:fetch).and_call_original
    allow(ENV).to receive(:fetch).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return("token")
    allow(Betterstack::LogDevice).to receive(:new).and_return(device)
    allow(device).to receive(:write).and_return(true)
  end

  it "adds a Better Stack logger at the Rails log level" do
    load initializer_path

    betterstack_logger = rails_logger.broadcasts.last
    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts.first).to be(stdout_logger)
    expect(betterstack_logger).to be_a(Logtail::Logger)
    expect(betterstack_logger.level).to eq(Logger::ERROR)
    expect(Betterstack::LogDevice).to have_received(:new).with("token", ingesting_host: "in.logs.example.com")
  end

  it "sends lines at or above the Rails log level to Better Stack and stdout" do
    load initializer_path

    rails_logger.warn("ignored")
    rails_logger.error("boom")

    expect(device).to have_received(:write).once.with(having_attributes(level: :error, message: "boom"))
    expect(stdout.string).to include("boom")
    expect(stdout.string).not_to include("ignored")
  end

  it "runs tagged blocks, like ActiveJob#perform_now, once" do
    load initializer_path
    runs = 0

    rails_logger.tagged("ActiveJob") do
      runs += 1
      rails_logger.error("inside a job")
    end

    expect(runs).to eq(1)
    expect(device).to have_received(:write).once
    expect(stdout.string).to include("[ActiveJob] inside a job")
  end

  it "falls back to logtail's default host when BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST is unset" do
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST").and_return(nil)

    load initializer_path

    expect(Betterstack::LogDevice).to have_received(:new).with("token", ingesting_host: nil)
  end

  it "does nothing without BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN" do
    allow(ENV).to receive(:[]).with("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN").and_return(nil)

    load initializer_path

    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts).to eq([stdout_logger])
  end

  it "does nothing outside production" do
    allow(Rails.env).to receive(:production?).and_return(false)

    load initializer_path

    expect(rails_logger.broadcasts).to eq([stdout_logger])
  end
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set, and the logtail gem isn't loaded otherwise.
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  betterstack_logger.level = Rails.logger.level

  # Exceptions Rails already turns into responses (404s, CSRF, routing, Pundit; see
  # rescue_responses) are logged with full traces. Keep them on stdout, not in Better Stack.
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)}) \(/
  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack { |entry| entry.message.to_s.match?(rescued_exception) }

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

content.text:
The new filter works: specs pass (7 of 7), rubocop is clean, and the spec fails without the filter. It's still uncommitted on the `betterstack-filter-rescued` branch.

**mlh-core does it differently** (`config/initializers/logtail.rb`):
```ruby
Rails.logger = Logtail::Logger.new(http_device, $stdout)   # Logtail is the main logger, stdout is secondary
```
- **Gem:** it uses `logtail-rails` (0.2.8), which adds structured request context but patches Rails' logging internals on load.
- **Level:** it ships at `info` (`production.rb:48`), not `error`.
- **Noise control at the source:** each chatty component is turned down to `warn` in its own initializer (Judoscale, Sidekiq, rack-timeout, the Sentry SDK logger), each with a comment about how much it was flooding Better Stack. There's no send-time filter.
- **Errors:** they go through Sentry and `BetterStack::ErrorMirror`, the same Sentry-to-Better-Stack approach as your draft #23595 for Forem.

**Is our approach best practice?** For Forem, yes. The differences from mlh-core are deliberate:
- **Plain `logtail`, not `logtail-rails`:** mlh-core owns its whole logging setup. Forem is open source and Datadog reads its stdout, so `logtail-rails` patching Rails' logging on every install is too invasive.
- **Adding a second destination, not replacing the logger:** Forem's stdout logger feeds Datadog and keeps its own formatting. mlh-core's setup makes stdout secondary to Logtail.
- **Filter at send time, not per-component levels:** mlh-core's per-component approach fixes noise from *chatty libraries at info/debug level*. Forem's noise is different: it's handled 404s, CSRF, routing and Pundit exceptions logged at `error`, so per-component levels can't reach it. The purely Rails fix is `log_rescued_responses = false`, but that would also strip them from Datadog, which you ruled out.
- **Where the filter's list comes from:** it builds from Rails' own `rescue_responses`, so it picks up new mappings in `config/application.rb` automatically. It drops a line only if the handled exception is the first thing in the message. A real error with a "Caused by: RecordNotFound" line still ships, and `ActiveRecord::QueryCanceled` isn't in the list, so statement timeouts still ship too.

**Worth adopting from mlh-core later:** its per-component `warn` pins. They'd matter if Forem ever raises `LOG_LEVEL` to `info`. At `error` they would be unused code, so I've left them out.

**Two things not covered by the filter:**
- **Template-digest errors:** the 54 "Couldn't find template for digesting: user_comments_sections/..." lines per 15 minutes are a real bug (a reference to a partial that doesn't exist). The filter doesn't touch them; they need a code fix.
- **Pasted secret:** my `heroku drains` output printed practicaldev's Datadog API key unredacted. My redaction missed the `dd-api-key=` parameter, and `.entire` pushes session checkpoints to the public `forem/forem` repo. Consider rotating that key.

Should I commit the filter and open the PR?

content.text:
It isn't dangerous, and it works well in mlh-core. For Forem it's the wrong trade: loading the gem changes Rails' logging for every Forem install, while the benefit it adds mostly goes unused at Forem's `error` log level.

**What it changes as soon as it's loaded.** I read the 0.2.12 source earlier. With a normal `gem "logtail-rails"` line, Bundler loads it in every environment for every install, whether or not a token is set:
1. **Patches `ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging`:** it changes how tags are formatted and how `add` works for every tagged logger. That includes the stdout logger Datadog reads.
2. **Replaces Rails' log subscribers** for ActionController, ActionView and ActiveRecord with its own structured versions.
3. **Silences `Rails::Rack::Logger`:** it points it at a null logger, which removes the "Started GET …" lines.
4. **Inserts 5 Rack middlewares:** HTTPContext, SessionContext, UserContext, HTTPEvents and ErrorEvent. They build context on every request, around 23k a minute on DEV, even when the log level then drops the output.
5. **Neutralizes Lograge and `rails_stdout_logging`** if either is present. Forem uses neither.
6. **Replaces Sidekiq's logger** if you use its `create_default_logger` helper, as its setup guide does.

**Why that's fine in mlh-core but not in Forem:**
- **Datadog's view:** mlh-core ships at `info` and Better Stack is its main log destination, so those structured request events are the point. Forem ships at `error` and Datadog reads its stdout, so items 1–3 change what Datadog sees in exchange for events that mostly never ship.
- **Other installs:** Forem is open source. Self-hosters who never use Better Stack would still get the patches and middlewares, which cuts against keeping each vendor optional.
- **Errors:** the one piece that would matter at `error` level is structured exceptions. Your #23595 (Sentry into Better Stack) already covers that, the same way mlh-core does it with `ErrorMirror`.

**It could be made safe:** use `require: false`, require it in `config/application.rb` only when the token is set (the Railtie has to be loaded before the app boots), and turn off the integrations you don't want with `Logtail::Integrations::Rails.enabled = false`. But then there's little left beyond what plain `logtail` already does, plus a gem that patches Rails internals to keep watching on upgrades.

I haven't measured the middleware overhead on DEV; that part is from reading the code. If you want structured request context in Better Stack later, use the gated setup above rather than a plain `gem "logtail-rails"` line.

content.text:
At Forem's `error` level, `logtail-rails` would add fields to the error lines we already ship, plus some request data that has privacy costs. Most of what it's known for is logged at `info`, so it would never ship. Here's each piece, from the gem source:

| What it adds | Ships at `error`? | Value vs. now |
|---|---|---|
| **HTTP context** on every line: host, method, path, client IP, request_id | yes, attached to error lines | **Real gain.** Today path and method only appear inside the message text, and request_id only as a `[uuid]` prefix. As fields, you could filter or alert on e.g. "errors on `/api/*`". The client IP is personal data. |
| **User context:** current user's id, name, **email** (from Warden/Devise) | yes | You could search errors by user. But it sends email addresses to a third party, bypassing Forem's `filter_parameters`, which filters `email`. I'd turn it off for DEV, and it's a bad default for other installs. |
| **Session context:** session id | yes | Marginal. |
| **Structured exceptions** (ErrorEvent): class, message and backtrace as fields, logged at `fatal` | yes | Would give cleaner grouping than multi-line text, but the Sentry path in #23595 does the same job better: grouping, fingerprints, deploy tracking. |
| **One event per request** (HTTPEvents): method, path, status, duration | **no**, logged at `info` | This is the headline feature and powers Better Stack's Rails dashboard. You'd have to go to `info`, which is about 23k lines a minute (≈33M a day). Datadog APM already has this per-request data. |
| **Controller, view and SQL events** replacing Rails' log subscribers | **no**, `info`/`debug` | Nothing at our level. |
| **Sidekiq job context** (job class, job id) | only on job lines that are errors | Minor. Datadog APM has it. |

**Net:** at our level the only unique win is structured path, method and request_id on error lines, and that comes with sending emails and IPs to Better Stack. The per-request events it's known for need `info`, which means ingest cost for data Datadog already has.

If structured path/method on errors is the part you want, a small Rack middleware can add it through plain `logtail`'s `Logtail.with_context`. That's about 10 lines, with no patches and no personal data. Worth doing, or leave it?

module Logtail
  module Integrations
    module ActionController
      class LogSubscriber < Integrator
        def initialize
          require "action_controller"
          require "action_controller/log_subscriber"
          require "logtail-rails/action_controller/log_subscriber/logtail_log_subscriber"
        rescue LoadError => e
          raise RequirementNotMetError.new(e.message)
        end
        def integrate!
          return true if Logtail::Integrations::Rails::ActiveSupportLogSubscriber.subscribed?(:action_controller, LogtailLogSubscriber)
          Logtail::Integrations::Rails::ActiveSupportLogSubscriber.unsubscribe!(:action_controller, ::ActionController::LogSubscriber)
          LogtailLogSubscriber.attach_to(:action_controller)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

begin
  require "action_dispatch/middleware/exception_wrapper"
rescue Exception
end
require "logtail/events/error"
require "logtail-rack/middleware"
require "logtail/util"
module Logtail
  module Integrations
    module Rails
      class ErrorEvent < Logtail::Integrations::Rack::Middleware
        EXCEPTION_WRAPPER_TAKES_CLEANER = defined?(::ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper) &&
          !::ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.instance_methods.include?(:env)
        def call(env)
          begin
            status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
          rescue Exception => exception
            Config.instance.logger.fatal do
              backtrace = extract_backtrace(env, exception)
              Events::Error.new(
                name: exception.class.name,
                error_message: exception.message,
                backtrace: backtrace
              )
            end
            raise exception
          end
        end
        private
        def extract_backtrace(env, exception)
          if defined?(::ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper)
            wrapper = if EXCEPTION_WRAPPER_TAKES_CLEANER
                        request = Util::Request.new(env)
                        backtrace_cleaner = request.get_header("action_dispatch.backtrace_cleaner")
                        ::ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.new(backtrace_cleaner, exception)
                      else
                        ::ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.new(env, exception)
                      end
            trace = wrapper.application_trace
            trace = wrapper.framework_trace if trace.empty?

begin
  require "active_support/tagged_logging"
  module Logtail
    module Overrides
      module ActiveSupportTaggedLogging
        module FormatterMethods
          def self.included(mod)
            mod.module_eval do
              alias_method :_logtail_original_push_tags, :push_tags
              alias_method :_logtail_original_pop_tags, :pop_tags
              def call(severity, timestamp, progname, msg)
                if is_a?(Logtail::Logger::Formatter)
                  super(severity, timestamp, progname, msg)
                else
                  super(severity, timestamp, progname, "#{tags_text}#{msg}")
                end
              end
            end
          end
        end
        module LoggerMethods
          def self.included(klass)
            klass.class_eval do
              def add(severity, message = nil, progname = nil, &block)
                if message.nil?
                  if block_given?
                    message = block.call
                  else
                    message = progname
                    progname = nil #No instance variable for this like Logger
                  end
                end
                if @logger.is_a?(Logtail::Logger)
                  @logger.add(severity, message, progname)
                else
                  @logger.add(severity, "#{tags_text}#{message}", progname)
                end
              end
            end
          end
        end
        if defined?(::ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging::Formatter)
          if !::ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging::Formatter.include?(FormatterMethods)
            ::ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging::Formatter.send(:include, FormatterMethods)
          end
        else
          if !::ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.include?(LoggerMethods)
            ::ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging.send(:include, LoggerMethods)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
rescue Exception
end
== integrator
module Logtail
  class Integrator
    class RequirementNotMetError < StandardError; end
    class << self
      attr_writer :enabled
      def enabled?
        @enabled != false
      end
      def integrate!(*args)
        if !enabled?
          Config.instance.debug_logger.debug("#{name} integration disabled, skipping") if Config.instance.debug_logger
          return false
        end
        new(*args).integrate!
        Config.instance.debug_logger.debug("Integrated #{name}") if Config.instance.debug_logger
        true
      rescue RequirementNotMetError => e
        Config.instance.debug_logger.debug("Failed integrating #{name}: #{e.message}") if Config.instance.debug_logger
        false
      end
    end
    def integrate!
      raise NotImplementedError.new
    end
  end
end

# Accessor method for {#custom_user_hash=}.
          def custom_user_hash
            @custom_user_hash
          end
        end
        def call(env)
          user_hash = get_user_hash(env)
          if user_hash
            CurrentContext.with({user: user_hash}) do
              @app.call(env)
            end
          else
            @app.call(env)
          end
        end
        private
          def get_user_hash(env)
            # The order is relevant here. The 'warden' key can be set, but
            # not return a user, in which case the user data might be in another key.
            if self.class.custom_user_hash.is_a?(Proc)
              Logtail::Config.instance.debug { "Obtaining user context from the custom user hash" }
              self.class.custom_user_hash.call(env)
            elsif env[:clearance] && env[:clearance].signed_in?
              Logtail::Config.instance.debug { "Obtaining user context from the clearance user" }
              user = env[:clearance].current_user
              get_user_object_hash(user)
            elsif env['warden'] && (user = env['warden'].user)
              Logtail::Config.instance.debug { "Obtaining user context from the warden user" }
              get_user_object_hash(user)
            else
              Logtail::Config.instance.debug { "Could not locate any user data" }
              nil
            end
          end
          def get_user_object_hash(user)
            id = try_user_id(user)
            name = try_user_name(user)
            email = try_user_email(user)
            if id || name || email
              {id: id, name: name, email: email}
            else
              nil
            end
          end
          def try_user_id(user)
            user.respond_to?(:id) ? user.id : nil
          end
          def try_user_name(user)
            if user.respond_to?(:name) && user.name.is_a?(String)
              user.name
            elsif user.respond_to?(:first_name) && user.first_name.is_a?(String) && user.respond_to?(:last_name) && user.last_name.is_a?(String)
              "#{user.first_name} #{user.last_name}"
            else
              nil
            end
          end
          def try_user_email(user)
            if user.respond_to?(:email) && user.email.is_a?(String)
              user.email
            else
              nil
            end
          end
      end
    end
  end
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set, and the logtail gem isn't loaded otherwise.
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  betterstack_logger.level = Rails.logger.level

  # Exceptions Rails already turns into responses (404s, CSRF, routing, Pundit; see
  # rescue_responses) are logged with full traces. Keep them on stdout, not in Better Stack.
  rescued_classes = Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{rescued_classes}) \(/
  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack { |entry| entry.message.to_s.match?(rescued_exception) }

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set; logtail-rails is only loaded then (config/application.rb).
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  # Set BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL=info to also get logtail-rails' per-request events; stdout keeps LOG_LEVEL.
  betterstack_logger.level = ENV["BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL"].presence&.to_sym || Rails.logger.level

  # logtail-rails' request and error events go only to Better Stack, so stdout keeps Rails' own lines.
  # Rails' log subscribers and Rack logger stay in place for the same reason.
  Logtail.config.logger = betterstack_logger
  [
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionController,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionView,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActiveRecord,
    Logtail::Integrations::Rails::RackLogger,
  ].each { |integration| integration.enabled = false }
  # Only the user's id: logtail-rack would otherwise send names and emails.
  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::UserContext.custom_user_hash = lambda do |env|
    (user = env["warden"]&.user) && { id: user.id }
  end

  # Exceptions Rails already turns into responses (404s, CSRF, routing, Pundit; see
  # rescue_responses) are logged with full traces. Keep them on stdout, not in Better Stack.
  rescued_classes = Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{rescued_classes}) \(/
  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack { |entry| entry.message.to_s.match?(rescued_exception) }

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set; logtail-rails is only loaded then (config/application.rb).
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  # Set BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL=info to also get logtail-rails' per-request events; stdout keeps LOG_LEVEL.
  betterstack_logger.level = ENV["BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL"].presence&.to_sym || Rails.logger.level

  # logtail-rails' request and error events go only to Better Stack, so stdout keeps Rails' own lines.
  # Rails' log subscribers and Rack logger stay in place for the same reason.
  Logtail.config.logger = betterstack_logger
  [
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionController,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionView,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActiveRecord,
    Logtail::Integrations::Rails::RackLogger,
  ].each { |integration| integration.enabled = false }
  # Only the user's id: logtail-rack would otherwise send names and emails.
  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::UserContext.custom_user_hash = lambda do |env|
    (user = env["warden"]&.user) && { id: user.id }
  end

  # Exceptions Rails already turns into responses (404s, CSRF, routing, Pundit; see
  # rescue_responses) are logged with full traces. Keep them on stdout, not in Better Stack.
  rescued_classes = Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{rescued_classes}) \(/
  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack { |entry| entry.message.to_s.match?(rescued_exception) }

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::UserContext.custom_user_hash = lambda do |env|

  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::HTTPEvents.http_header_filters = %w[

  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::HTTPEvents.collapse_into_single_event = true

  rescued_classes = Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{rescued_classes}) \(/

  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack do |entry|

  end

# Ship production logs to Better Stack as well as to the existing logger (stdout on Heroku).
# Off unless BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN is set; logtail-rails is only loaded then (config/application.rb).
if Rails.env.production? && ENV["BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"].present?
  require Rails.root.join("lib/betterstack/log_device")

  betterstack_logger = Logtail::Logger.new(
    Betterstack::LogDevice.new(
      ENV.fetch("BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN"),
      # Falls back to logtail's default host when unset.
      ingesting_host: ENV["BETTERSTACK_INGESTING_HOST"].presence,
    ),
  )
  # Set BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL=info to also get logtail-rails' per-request events; stdout keeps LOG_LEVEL.
  betterstack_logger.level = ENV["BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL"].presence&.to_sym || Rails.logger.level

  # logtail-rails' request events go only to Better Stack, so stdout keeps Rails' own lines.
  # Rails' log subscribers and Rack logger stay in place for the same reason. ErrorEvent is off
  # because Rails already logs every unhandled exception; it would ship each one twice.
  Logtail.config.logger = betterstack_logger
  [
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionController,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActionView,
    Logtail::Integrations::ActiveRecord,
    Logtail::Integrations::Rails::RackLogger,
    Logtail::Integrations::Rails::ErrorEvent,
  ].each { |integration| integration.enabled = false }
  # Only the user's id: logtail-rack would otherwise send names and emails.
  Logtail::Integrations::Rack::UserContext.custom_user_hash = lambda do |env|
    (user = env["warden"]&.user) && { id: user.id }
  end

  # Exceptions Rails already turns into responses (404s, CSRF, routing, Pundit; see
  # rescue_responses) are logged with full traces. Keep them on stdout, not in Better Stack.
  rescued_classes = Regexp.union(ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses.keys)
  rescued_exception = /\A\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:#{rescued_classes}) \(/
  Logtail.config.filter_sent_to_better_stack { |entry| entry.message.to_s.match?(rescued_exception) }

  # Logtail::Logger must not respond to #tagged: BroadcastLogger runs a tagged block once per
  # logger that does, so ActiveJob#perform_now would run every job twice.
  Rails.logger.broadcast_to(betterstack_logger)
end

content.text:
`logtail-rails` is now wired in with Datadog's stdout unchanged. It's uncommitted on the `betterstack-filter-rescued` branch, together with the noise filter. I checked it by booting production mode on my machine and sending real test lines to the DEV.to Better Stack source, and the specs pass (8 of 8).

**What changed:**
- **`Gemfile` / `Gemfile.lock`:** `logtail` is replaced by `logtail-rails` with `require: false`. I restored 3 unrelated `vendor/cache` gems (rbs, ruby-lsp, ruby-lsp-rails) that `bundle install` had deleted. The two new logtail gems in `vendor/cache` are untracked and need adding to the commit.
- **`config/application.rb`:** the gem is required only in production with `BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN` set. Without the token, no Logtail middleware is added (checked).
- **`config/initializers/betterstack.rb`:**
  - The gem's events go only to Better Stack.
  - Rails' log subscribers and Rack logger stay in place.
  - ErrorEvent is off, because Rails already logs each unhandled exception once.
  - User context sends only the user ID.
  - Credential headers are filtered: `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `api-key`, `x-algolia-api-key`, `health-check-token`, CSRF token.
  - The noise filter now also drops Rails' duplicate request lines.
  - A new `BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL` sets Better Stack's level separately from stdout's.

**What I checked:**
- **stdout is unchanged:** production-mode boots with and without the gem print identical tagged, pushed and plain lines.
- **Jobs still run once:** tagged blocks (how ActiveJob runs a job) execute once.
- **Middleware order:** the Logtail middlewares sit after `RequestId` and `Warden`.
- **Request context:** every Better Stack line in a request carries `context.http` (host, method, path, client IP, request_id).
- **No secrets:** a request with fake cookie, API-key and bearer values sent none of them to Better Stack.
- **At `info`:** each request produces 2 Better Stack lines, the `Processing by Controller#action` line and one request event. Before the tuning it was 6.

**Volume:**
- **At the default (Rails' `error` level):** about 12 lines a minute, mostly statement timeouts plus the template-digest bug, which needs a separate view fix. At this level you mostly get the request context on errors.
- **With `BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL=info`:** you'd also get per-request events, about 2 lines per request. At 23k requests a minute that's roughly 46k lines a minute (about 66M a day). Check the Better Stack plan before switching it on.

**Two things to know:**
- **Test suite:** the spec loads `logtail-rails`, so its `TaggedLogging` patch is active for the rest of the test run. It produced identical output in my comparison.
- **The header filter is a blocklist:** any new credential header will need adding to it.

Should I commit and open the draft PR?

cd /Users/jonmarkgo/Documents/GitHub/forem; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jonmarkgo-Documents-GitHub-forem/bf9fb0a8-fe46-4a1d-a775-84fde1733cdb/scratchpad/pr2.md <<'EOF'
## What

This switches Better Stack logging from plain `logtail` to `logtail-rails`, so Better Stack lines get request context. It also cuts the noise we've been seeing in the DEV.to source. stdout, and so Datadog, stays the same.

It still only runs in production with `BETTERSTACK_SOURCE_TOKEN` set. The gem is `require: false` and is only required in `config/application.rb` when that token is set, so other Forem installs never load it.

## What Better Stack gets now
- `context.http` on every line inside a request: host, method, path, client IP, request_id
- `context.user` with the user's **id only**; `logtail-rack` would otherwise send name and email
- at `info` (opt-in, see below): one structured request event per request (method, path, status, duration)

## Keeping stdout/Datadog unchanged
- `Logtail.config.logger` points at the Better Stack logger, so the gem's request events never go to stdout.
- The ActionController, ActionView and ActiveRecord integrations and the RackLogger integration are off. Rails' own log subscribers and `Rails::Rack::Logger` stay in place.
- ErrorEvent is off, because Rails already logs every unhandled exception and it would ship each one twice. Structured errors are #23595's job (Sentry).
- The one global effect left is the `TaggedLogging` patch applied when the gem loads. I booted production mode locally with and without the token, and tagged, `push_tags` and plain lines came out byte-identical.
- Tagged blocks still run once (the ActiveJob double-run guard from #23878).

## Noise
In a 15-minute sample of the DEV.to source, about 95% of lines were exceptions Rails already turns into responses: `RecordNotFound`, CSRF, `RoutingError`, Pundit. The filter drops a line when one of those classes (`ActionDispatch::ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses`) is the exception at the start of the message. That means:
- new mappings in `config/application.rb` are picked up automatically
- a real error with a `Caused by: RecordNotFound` line still ships
- `QueryCanceled` isn't in the list, so statement timeouts still ship

Those lines stay on stdout. At `info`, Rails' `Started` / `Parameters` / `Completed` lines are also kept out of Better Stack because the request event duplicates them. The `Processing by Controller#action` line stays.

From that sample, what would still ship at `error` is about 12 lines/min: statement timeouts (~8/min), a template-digest bug (`render user_comments_section` in `users/_main_feed`, separate fix), Rack timeouts, OAuth failures, a `media_stores` NotNullViolation.

## Headers
Request events record headers, and `logtail-rack` filters none by default. This PR filters `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-CSRF-Token`, `api-key`, `x-algolia-api-key` and `health-check-token`. It's a denylist, so any new credential header needs adding here.

## New env var
`BETTERSTACK_LOG_LEVEL` (optional) sets the Better Stack level separately from `LOG_LEVEL`. It defaults to the Rails level (`error` on DEV). Setting it to `info` turns on per-request events: about 2 lines per request, so check the Better Stack plan first.

## Testing
- `spec/initializers/betterstack_spec.rb` (8 examples)
  - new: gem events are routed only to Better Stack, integrations are off, user context is id only
  - new: rescued-exception filter (this spec fails without the filter)
- Local production-mode boot against the real source:

- `context.user` with the user's **id only**; `logtail-rack` would otherwise send name and email
- at `info` (opt-in, see below): one structured request event per request (method, path, status, duration)

## Keeping stdout/Datadog unchanged
- `Logtail.config.logger` points at the Better Stack logger, so the gem's request events never go to stdout.
- The ActionController, ActionView and ActiveRecord integrations and the RackLogger integration are off. Rails' own log subscribers and `Rails::Rack::Logger` stay in place.
- ErrorEvent is off, because Rails already logs every unhandled exception and it would ship each one twice. Structured errors are #23595's job (Sentry).

In a 15-minute sample of the DEV.to source, about 95% of lines were exceptions Rails already turns into responses: `RecordNotFound`, CSRF, `RoutingError`, Pundit. Request events record headers, and `logtail-rack` filters none by default. This PR filters `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-CSRF-Token`, `api-key`, `x-algolia-api-key` and `health-check-token`. It's a denylist, so any new credential header needs adding here.
